{{Short description|American physicist and author}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2020}}
'''Harvey Einbinder''' (June 18, 1926 – January 30, 2013)<ref name="legacy-obit" /> was an American [[physicist]], [[author]] and amateur historian.

== Early life ==
Einbinder was born to Jacob B. Einbinder and Dora (née Abelson) in [[New Haven, Connecticut]].<ref name=legacy-obit>[<!-- http://obituaries/nhregister/obituary.aspx?pid=162780231 -->https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/nhregister/name/harvey-einbinder-obituary?id=18578456 Harvey Einbinder], legacy.com</ref> He had one brother, David, and one sister, Hinde.<ref name=j-ledg>[http://www.jewishledger.com/2013/02/einbinder/ EINBINDER] Obituaries ''Jewish Ledger'' (Connecticut), February 5, 2013. Retrieved September 22, 2014</ref>

== Education ==
Einbinder studied for two years at the [[University of Connecticut]] (UConn), at first physics but then mathematics in which he received a degree with "highest distinction" in 1946.<ref name=uc-math/> He later received his Ph.D. in physics from [[Columbia University]].

== Career ==
He became a consultant to the [[Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory]] and to General Electric on the [[Atlas missile]].<ref name="uc-math" /> He published papers on [[Hypersonic speed|hypersonic aerodynamics]] and the ionization of solid particles.<ref name="uc-math">{{cite journal |last=Einbinder |first=Harvey |date=Spring 2000 |title=THE EARLY YEARS AT UCONN |url=http://www.math.uconn.edu/wp-content/uploads/newsletter/mathconnections2000.pdf |url-status=dead |journal=Math CONNections-A Newsletter from the UConn Mathematics Department |publisher=University of Connecticut |volume=3 |pages=8, 13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160615095839/http://www.math.uconn.edu/wp-content/uploads/newsletter/mathconnections2000.pdf |archive-date=2016-06-15 |accessdate=September 22, 2014}}</ref><ref name="doi=10.1063/1.1698931">{{cite journal |last1=Einbinder |first1=Harvey |title=The Hydrodynamic Stability of Flame Fronts |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |date=1 March 1953 |volume=21 |issue=3 |pages=480–489 |doi=10.1063/1.1698931}}</ref><ref name="doi=10.1063/1.1698800">{{cite journal |last1=Einbinder |first1=Harvey |title=The Application of Jacobians to Statistical Thermodynamics |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |date=1 December 1953 |volume=21 |issue=12 |pages=2134–2142 |doi=10.1063/1.1698800}}</ref> Einbinder patented a ten-finger typewriter keyboard.<ref name="patent/US4332493A">{{cite web |last1=Einbinder |first1=Harvey |title=Ten-finger typewriter keyboards |url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US4332493A/en |website=US patent |access-date=23 July 2023 |date=1 June 1982}}</ref>

== Encyclopædia Britannica ==
Einbinder spent five years combing the ''[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]'' for flaws, and found enough to fill a 390-page book, called ''The Myth of the Britannica'', published by [[Grove Press]] in 1964.<ref name=brit-myth>Einbinder, Harvey ''[https://books.google.com/books?id=H9oqnQEACAAJ&q=The+Myth+of+the+Britannica.+New+York:+Grove+Press,+1964+/+London:+MacGibbon+%26+Kee,+1964+/+New+York:+Johnson+Reprint+Corp.,+1972 The Myth of the Britannica]''. New York: [[Grove Press]], 1964 (OCLC 152581687)/ London: MacGibbon & Kee, 1964 (OCLC 807782651) / New York: Johnson Reprint Corp., 1972. (OCLC 286856)</ref> As summarized by ''[[The Age]]'' two years later, Einbinder's book "showed beyond argument that the Britannica was not a completely impartial and absolutely infallible work of general reference; that 666 articles in the 1963 edition were reprinted from editions dating back to 1875 in some cases; and that American influence on its editorial policy had become dominant".<ref>Peter Westcott ''[https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=DEoQAAAAIBAJ&sjid=XpMDAAAAIBAJ&pg=3633,4887304 Britannica on the Shelves]'' (review of the 1965 edition of Encyclopædia Britannica), The Age, May 28, 1966, p.25</ref> The Science Magazine commended Einbinder as a "dedicated prince of iconoclasts" who "rips into his subject from all angles and with devastating effect".<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Brooke-Hitching |first=Edward |title=The madman's library: the strangest books, manuscripts and other literary curiosities from history |date=2020 |publisher=Simon & Schuster |isbn=978-1-4711-6692-1 |location=London New York Sydney Toronto New Delhi}}</ref> Furthermore, it was suggested that the editorial board of the [[Encyclopædia  Britannica]] hire Einbinder as a fact-checker, although this never came to be.<ref name=":0" /> 

Einbinder at one point also disputed the historical accuracy of the [[Black Hole of Calcutta]] account.{{Cn|date=June 2024}} Among his other publications are ''An American Genius: [[Frank Lloyd Wright]]'', and the play ''Mah Name is Lyndon'' (about US president [[Lyndon B. Johnson]] and the [[Vietnam War]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mah name is Lyndon; a play. Illustrated by Florence Safadi - Catalogue |url=https://catalogue.nla.gov.au/catalog/2098438 |access-date=2024-06-04 |website=catalogue.nla.gov.au |publisher=National Library of Australia |language=en}}</ref>).

== Private life ==
Harvey Einbinder was married to Florence Einbinder, who predeceased him. He died on January 30, 2013, at [[Mount Sinai Hospital (Manhattan)|Mt. Sinai Hospital]] in New York City.<ref name=j-ledg/>
